entities.name: Maximus the Confessor
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Maximus the Confessor (c. 580–662) was a Byzantine monk-theologian whose resistance to Monothelitism, profound spiritual writings, and eventual mutilation and exile made him a defining voice of Chalcedonian Orthodoxy. Serving briefly in imperial administration before monastic life, he developed a cosmic Christology of the logoi and deification.

At the Lateran Council of 649 and in disputes with Constans II’s court, Maximus defended two wills in Christ. Tortured and dying in exile, he earned the title Confessor; later councils vindicated his theology.

He remains a pillar of Eastern Christian mystical and dogmatic tradition.
